  to the Red Sea, which shortened the voyage from Europe to
  Asia by thousands of miles. The Panama Canal followed in
  1914 after a failed French attempt and a huge American
  effort that fought disease as much as terrain. Both
  reshaped world trade, and both became flashpoints of
  geopolitics.

  Today many old leisure canals have been restored for
  boating, walking and wildlife, while the great ship canals
  still carry a large share of global commerce. From
  irrigation ditches to international shipping lanes, canals
  show a steady human ambition to redirect water to suit
  human purposes.
